changeEvents.title: Coding Harness Apps
changeEvents.description: An app whose backend is an agentic harness, and whose interface exists to collect the one thing the harness cannot do itself. Coding harness apps, or CHAPPS. The harness runs the pipeline, summons a real interface when it needs your hands, eyes, or voice, then takes the data back and keeps going.

changeEvents.title: Harness Apps
changeEvents.description: An app whose entire backend is an agentic harness. Harness apps, or happs. Commonly called Claude Code apps: small purpose-built interfaces, often temporary, where the buttons are wired to Claude Code or Codex rather than to a server you wrote.

changeEvents.title: Local-First Software
changeEvents.description: Software that runs and keeps its data on your own machine. In the agentic era, a bespoke tool per problem becomes cheap enough to build, use once, and throw away.

changeEvents.title: Skill File First, App Second
changeEvents.description: If you want to build a capability that operates on people's context, prove it as a skill file first. Package it as an app only after the capability is real.

changeEvents.title: The Harness Should Be Your Default Interface
changeEvents.description: Most people open an app and do the work by hand. The better default is to start in an agentic harness, describe the outcome, and let the harness open an interface only for the steps that need your body.

changeEvents.title: The Evangelist Sees the Frontier Before the Lab Does
changeEvents.description: What a model can do is settled in a lab. What it is for is discovered in contact with a specific job, by whoever is standing there. That makes the person deployed into real builds the first to know, and it means an evangelist who is not also an inventor is mis-hired.

changeEvents.title: Agent Rule Files
changeEvents.description: Standing orders the agent reads at the start of every session. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Imperative, persistent, always-on. The version-controlled spine of how an agent behaves inside your workspace.

changeEvents.title: Compounding Docs
changeEvents.description: Every document you write makes your AI agent smarter. Every smarter agent output makes the next document faster. The flywheel nobody talks about.

changeEvents.title: Context Engineering
changeEvents.description: The discipline of curating the right information state for an AI system to operate within. The skill that separates 'AI is okay' from 'AI changed how I work.'

changeEvents.title: Harness Engineering
changeEvents.description: The code wrapped around an AI model is just as important as the model itself. The discipline of designing that wrapper.

changeEvents.title: Spec Writing
changeEvents.description: The discipline of describing what you want with enough precision that an AI can deliver it. Implementation is being commoditized; the spec is where the value lives now.

changeEvents.description: The seventeen layers standing between a human value and a deployed model's output. No layer repairs a misalignment above it, which makes choosing your upstream the decision that sets your ceiling.

changeEvents.title: The Correction Seam
changeEvents.description: The boundary between two products where one makes an error and the other collects the user's correction of it. The signal is free, self-labeling, and unusable by either company alone, which turns an ordinary build-versus-buy question into a decision about whether to close a loop.

changeEvents.title: Weight Training Data by Who Is Still in Business
changeEvents.description: Once a system learns from user corrections, it has to decide whose corrections count. Every available proxy for good judgment is bad, and money is the least bad of them, because a customer who keeps paying has run an expensive test you get to inherit for free.

The signal is free, self-labeling, and unusable by either company alone, which turns an ordinary build-versus-buy question into a decision about whether to close a loop.

changeEvents.title: Onboarding Belongs in a Repo That Holds Your State
changeEvents.description: The friction in adopting new AI infrastructure is that nobody holds your state between sessions. Ship the onboarding as a project the developer clones, which tracks real integration instead of lessons read.

changeEvents.title: Anatomy
changeEvents.description: The four load-bearing components inside every SOP Execution App: a page per SOP with a form per page, role-scoped memory drawn from the team layer, role-scoped views, and a backend of agents.

changeEvents.title: PE fund cascade
changeEvents.description: One retainer at the PE-fund level becomes many AI transformation engagements across the portfolio. The buyer pattern that multiplies the three-month POC wedge.

changeEvents.title: Three-month POC as the PE-fund cascade wedge
changeEvents.description: The MBB playbook is now open-source. A boutique AI consultancy operator walks through the structure he runs against PE funds: $9K-$30K retainers, three-month proof of concept, year-long engagement after.

changeEvents.title: BOI on AI strategy: blueprint, not backlog
changeEvents.description: Field notes from a November 2024 BOI webinar with Philippe De Ridder and Vincent Pirenne. Three Waves of AI adoption, outside-in plus future-back, the AI Opportunity Radar, and why AI alone is not a moat.

changeEvents.title: bycloud on DeepSeek V4: efficiency is the whole strategy
changeEvents.description: Field notes from bycloud's breakdown of the DeepSeek V4 technical report. Cheap million-token context, cost-performance over benchmark-maxing, the bottleneck that just keeps moving, and serving reliability as the real constraint at scale.

changeEvents.title: Caleb Curry: stop instructing the agent, start gating it
changeEvents.description: Field notes from Caleb Curry's six months building a multi-tenant SaaS with Claude Code. His breakthrough was converting written rules into deterministic gates: linting, types, database adapters, and hooks the agent cannot interpret its way past.

changeEvents.title: The Playbook for a $100M AI Agency
changeEvents.description: Devin Karns of Custom AI Studio on why mid-market is the AI era's sweet spot, why services firms re-rate from 1x to 5x EBITDA at the $5M threshold, and the four-step engagement ladder that takes contracts from $5k to $1M+.

changeEvents.title: Frank Coyle: hallucination is the feature, so build the rails around it
changeEvents.description: Field notes from a talk on why agentic systems need ontologies. The neural half imagines and the symbolic half refuses, and the architecture that wires them together already has a name and a fifty-year history.

changeEvents.title: Goldratt: management attention is the ultimate constraint
changeEvents.description: Field notes from Rami Goldratt's webinar carrying his father's final-years thesis. Management attention is the binding constraint of every organization, and three killers waste it: chasing symptoms, living in a compromise, and chasing targets instead of enablers.

changeEvents.title: The $1M AI job: the Forward Deployed Engineer, explained
changeEvents.description: Field notes from Greg Isenberg's interview with Voss (Veric Agents). Intelligence is commoditized; the edge is deployment. The FDE is the person who bridges general intelligence and one company's specific reality, plus a 30-day plan to become one.

changeEvents.title: IndyDevDan: forget loop engineering, build AI developer workflows
changeEvents.description: Field notes from IndyDevDan's case against 'loop engineering.' The loop is one node. The real unit is the AI developer workflow: the right combination of engineers, agents, and code, composed up into a software factory.

changeEvents.title: The arrogance of developers, and the token-max compulsion
changeEvents.description: First-person fieldwork on why developers over-build solved infrastructure, why spending tokens feels like progress when it is not, and the identity shift from vibe coder to operator who buys what is already solved.

changeEvents.title: The Wisdom Crisis: What LLMs Are Actually Doing to Us
changeEvents.description: John Vervaeke and Jonathan Pageau on AI's civilizational stakes: model collapse, the Moloch trap, the ontological mismatch, and why wisdom education is the only durable response.

changeEvents.title: YC on the self-improving company
changeEvents.description: Field notes from a May 2026 YC Root Access talk. The Roman-legion company is over. Reimagine the company as recursive self-improving AI loops. ICs and DRIs only. Burn tokens, not headcount. Right for net-new orgs, far-fetched for legacy dinosaurs.

changeEvents.title: YC on building an AI-native services company
changeEvents.description: Field notes from a June 2026 YC founder playbook. Rebuild services firms (law, tax, insurance) so AI does most of the work and you sell the finished outcome, not a copilot. The human is the interface; the operation is the product. Right for net-new orgs, a thought experiment for incumbents.

changeEvents.title: Claire Vo
changeEvents.description: Founder of ChatPRD, host of How I AI, three-time chief product officer. The clearest working example of a profitable business staffed by a constellation of scoped agents.

changeEvents.title: Cory Doctorow
changeEvents.description: Author and activist who coined the popular usage of 'reverse centaur' for AI deployments that subordinate the human to the machine. Public-teaching source on the labor and capital failure modes of the AI bubble.

changeEvents.title: Daniel Priestley
changeEvents.description: Founder of Dent Global and ScoreApp. Author of Key Person of Influence and Oversubscribed. Public-teaching source on how entrepreneurs reprice their work in the post-AI economy.

changeEvents.title: Satya Nadella
changeEvents.description: Chairman and CEO of Microsoft. Public-teaching source on what becomes valuable in the age of token abundance: cognitive coverage, token intelligence, and the human skills that compound alongside agents.

changeEvents.title: My AI Assistant Can't See My App's Memory or Project Folders. How Do You Deal With That?
changeEvents.description: The friction is real and it is not a skill issue. It is the moment you decide whether to keep renting someone else's memory system or cross the chasm and own your context layer.

changeEvents.title: AI Advisor to the CEO
changeEvents.description: The cross-organizational pattern-recognizer the CEO retains personally. Wide context across many companies, deep experience inside several, and direct counsel at the moments when the wrong AI decision would cost the entire business.

changeEvents.title: AI Enablement Architect
changeEvents.description: The person who deploys company-wide AI upskilling infrastructure: platform, skill marketplace, integrations, and adoption mechanics.

changeEvents.title: The AI Guide
changeEvents.description: The trusted person people go to when they want to know what to do about AI. Advisory at large scale, to anyone. The load-bearing pillar of the AI economy, because trust is the real bottleneck.

changeEvents.title: The AI-Services Founder
changeEvents.description: The founder profile for an AI-native services company: domain fluency, model fluency, and operational rigor. The unglamorous third trait is the differentiator, because the product is an operation.

changeEvents.title: Applied AI Streamliner
changeEvents.description: The implementer who builds hyper-personalized software for individual professionals. They sit with the person, decompose their daily workflows, and build custom apps that wrap agentic capabilities around exactly how that person works.

changeEvents.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
changeEvents.description: The Palantir-coined seat that turns commoditized intelligence into working systems inside one company's messy reality. The rare person who is genuinely excellent at both the business and the code, not the average of the two.

changeEvents.title: Generative Experience Architect
changeEvents.description: The seat a subject-matter expert steps into when they stop delivering their expertise one client at a time and start designing the system that generates it. They are accountable for the felt quality of every outcome the system produces.

changeEvents.title: Leader As Workflow PM
changeEvents.description: When the workforce becomes a collective of humans plus agents plus robots, leadership starts to look like product management. Leaders manage workflows and products, not people and processes.

changeEvents.title: Executive Summary
changeEvents.description: The applied-AI worldview this wiki encodes, in one page. The load-bearing claims about the economy, the interface, the strategy, and the operator that a practitioner should know cold.

changeEvents.title: Why You Should Learn to Wield AI
changeEvents.description: The foundational both/and for anyone who found this wiki while worried: AI is a way for people who care about their work to do a better job, and the honest risk to your livelihood is a person in your field who wields it.

changeEvents.title: A Bias for Iteration Is the Price of Admission Now
changeEvents.description: Comfort with rapid, real-time iteration used to be a temperament. It is now the entry requirement for building products at all. The people who win iterate fast, learn quickly, and build systems that learn, on a substrate that is itself improving underneath them.

changeEvents.title: A Corpus Plus a Form Is Most of the Book
changeEvents.description: When a life is captured as an annotated corpus and a story form is specified as a buildable artifact, an agentic production process can carry a book to 80 to 90 percent done. The human's remaining job is detailed editing and judgment.

changeEvents.title: A Moved Measurable Is the Only Proof
changeEvents.description: The proof your AI work is real is that it moves a load-bearing, profit-tied measurable the business already agreed matters. Everything else is novelty at best, and AI is happy to help you mistake it for traction.

changeEvents.title: A Startup Is an Outcome Generator
changeEvents.description: A startup is a company whose product reliably produces a valued outcome on demand. Accelerators are factories that manufacture outcome generators, and the frontier labs are the power source underneath all of them.

changeEvents.title: Acceleration Is Not Completion
changeEvents.description: AI has meaningfully accelerated code production. That is different from coding being solved. Collapsing the two is a category error with real costs for operators who build toward the wrong capability.

changeEvents.title: Agents Compress Work Onto Your Judgment
changeEvents.description: AI agents do not reduce work. They compress it. The compression lands on the one layer that does not scale: human judgment.

changeEvents.title: Agents Read READMEs
changeEvents.description: Keep agent rule files thin and push the substance into a genuinely good README the rule file points at. Agents read READMEs the way capable developers do.

changeEvents.title: AGI Is Already Here for People Who Can Wield It
AI Discourse Refuses to Name Its Political Reality
changeEvents.description: The obvious political reality that AI discourse keeps refusing to name: the flaming red elephant in the room. Red for the revolutionary spirit rising in a generation locked out of the economy. Flaming for the firebombs already being thrown at AI executives and data centers. Elephant because the cause is obvious and nobody at the top of the industry wants to look at it.

changeEvents.title: AI Eats Labor Allocation
changeEvents.description: SaaS captured a tiny slice of corporate budgets (the software allocation). AI captures a much larger slice (the labor allocation). The unit economics are 50-100x different, and they explain why AI consulting firms can re-rate faster than legacy services firms.

changeEvents.title: AI Is Becoming the Thing We Serve
changeEvents.description: We built AI to serve us. We are ending up serving it. The ancient pattern of the idol is playing out in real time: the thing made to extend human power becomes the thing humans serve.

changeEvents.title: AI Is Your Smartest, Most Coachable Friend Who Has Read Everything But Experienced Nothing
changeEvents.description: The fastest accurate model of AI: a brilliant friend with no lived experience and no internal compass for truth. It is wildly coachable in either direction, which is why the operator's lived experience and discerning taste are the load-bearing inputs.

changeEvents.title: AI-Native Org Charts Put Humans at the Edges
changeEvents.description: In an AI-native company, the AI sits in the center: the company brain, the data, the skills, the loops. Humans live at the perimeter, interfacing with reality where the intelligence makes contact with the world. The org chart inverts.

changeEvents.title: Applied AI Pays Off Where Fit Is Already Proven
changeEvents.description: Applied AI pays off fastest inside a business that has already proven market fit, where it clears bottlenecks and compounds profit. Spinning up a speculative AI startup in today's crowded, bubbly market is a far worse use of the same energy.

changeEvents.title: Buyers Fumble Alone Before They Hire You
changeEvents.description: People try to figure out AI alone on minimal spend, fumble for months, then hire a coach. The lag between starting solo and reaching out is the consultant's sales-timing signal.

changeEvents.title: Capability Is Table Stakes, Faithfulness Is the Choice
changeEvents.description: The bar for choosing an agentic stack is faithfulness: acting in the spirit of your mission when your instructions run out, and sometimes holding you to a higher standard than you asked for.

changeEvents.title: The More Capable the Agent, the More Guardrails It Needs
changeEvents.description: A capable agent's failure mode is not stupidity, it is confident, plausible shortcutting. The smarter it is, the more convincing the wrong thing it ships. Guardrails are how you get quality out of it, and the need for them rises with capability.

changeEvents.title: Commercial Success Selects for Truthful Models
changeEvents.description: For AI that is paid to do a job, the market's success signal and the truth signal are the same thing: whether the customer got what they actually wanted. So winning the market selects for models that are reliable and honest. This holds only where the product is bought to complete a task, not to hold attention, where the selection runs the opposite way.

changeEvents.title: Crossing $5M Revenue Re-Rates a Services Firm
changeEvents.description: Services businesses sell at 1-2x EBITDA below roughly $5M annual revenue and 4-5x EBITDA above it. The same multiple jump applies to AI consulting firms. The threshold is the structural reason the exit posture decision matters.

changeEvents.title: Daily Use Is the Benchmark That Can't Be Gamed
changeEvents.description: A published benchmark is a target a vendor can train to. Months of daily use by a demanding operator is an eval nobody can see, so nobody can game it. Trust the felt experience, and the revealed preference of builders you respect, over the leaderboard.

changeEvents.title: Demonstration Is the Highest-Bandwidth Spec
changeEvents.description: Three minutes of doing a workflow while narrating it carries more usable specification than an hour of writing the procedure down. The binding constraint on automating a process was never model capability. It was asking an operator to describe something their hands run without conscious observation.

changeEvents.title: Deny Rules Are Not a Wall
changeEvents.description: Permission rules steer an agent toward the right default and persist across sessions, which is worth having. They cannot contain an agent, because the same action has many spellings. If an outcome is unacceptable, remove the capability rather than writing a rule against it.

changeEvents.title: Developers Have Started Worshipping the Build
changeEvents.description: Developers have started worshipping the act of building over the outcome it is supposed to serve. Spending tokens feels like progress. It is not. The business only ever paid for the outcome, and most of the outcome is already solved.

changeEvents.title: The Default AI Move Is to Document and Streamline Load-Bearing Workflows
changeEvents.description: Whatever else you do with AI, the no-regret baseline every business owes itself is to document its load-bearing workflows and streamline them. It is the floor, not the ceiling. Every fancier bet sits on top of a mapped operation or it sits on sand.

changeEvents.title: Efficiency Wins Do Not Predict New-Category Wins
changeEvents.description: AI adoption follows the same three-wave shape every prior general-purpose technology took. Wave 1 squeezes efficiency from existing workflows. Wave 2 raises quality. Wave 3 invents new categories. Wave 1 success does not predict Wave 3 success.

changeEvents.title: Every AI Business Model Has a Different Ceiling
changeEvents.description: A working chart of every distinct business model for monetizing AI expertise in 2026, plotted on technical depth against contract size. Each model has a different ceiling, a different exit profile, and a different operational shape. Pick deliberately.

changeEvents.title: Every Brand Should Be a Version-Controlled Universe Its Agent Renders on Demand
changeEvents.description: The brand book is a dead PDF the moment it ships. The alternative is a brand held as a version-controlled universe an agent loads and renders on demand, so a partner can browse it, a creator can generate from it, and an operator can edit it, all in plain language, all from one source of truth.

changeEvents.title: Every Company Is Quietly Sorting Its People
Execution Is No Longer What You Get Paid For
changeEvents.description: Daniel Priestley's framing of post-AI work. AI tokens replace task execution, so humans get paid for conviction, judgment, taste, commercial outcomes, and improving the system.

changeEvents.title: Frameworks Are Proven by Variety, Not Volume
changeEvents.description: A framework that has produced one kind of thing a hundred times is still unproven. Each new KIND of instance is what exposes a structural hole, and review never finds them because review only checks internal coherence.

changeEvents.title: Generation Is Cheap, Discrimination Is the Job
Great Work Is a Byproduct of Volume Plus Taste
Improvement Compounds When the Loops Nest
changeEvents.description: One improvement loop is table stakes. The compounding move is a loop at every level of abstraction, nested, with lessons flowing up and work flowing down. Each level catches what the level below cannot see, including the loop that grades the grader.

changeEvents.title: Intelligence Is Commoditized, Deployment Is the Moat
changeEvents.description: Every company can buy the same frontier intelligence, so intelligence is no longer the edge. The advantage moved to deployment: the bridge between general intelligence and one company's specific processes, politics, and exceptions.

changeEvents.title: Knowing AI Changes How You Use It
changeEvents.description: The more someone knows about AI, the less casually they use it. Expertise doesn't produce more adoption; it produces more discriminating use. One of the most diagnostic signals about what AI actually is.

changeEvents.title: Lifestyle or Enterprise Value Is a Day-One Decision
changeEvents.description: The decision every AI consulting founder makes in their first month, usually without naming it. Lifestyle businesses and enterprise-value businesses look the same on day 30 and look completely different on day 730. Choose deliberately.

changeEvents.title: LLMs Handle Judgment, Code Handles Everything Else
Making One Layer Cheap Just Moves the Bottleneck
changeEvents.description: Make one layer cheap and the binding constraint does not disappear. It relocates. Efficiency is a frontier you keep advancing, not a finish line you cross once.

changeEvents.title: Mid-Market Executives Are Buying a Narrative
changeEvents.description: Mid-market executives are not buying AI systems. They are buying a coherent narrative they can take to their board, their team, and themselves. The technology is downstream of the narrative. Once you see this, your sales calls change.

changeEvents.title: Mid-Markets Are the AI Sweet Spot
changeEvents.description: Mid-market companies ($10M-$250M annual revenue) are the AI era's prime client profile for consulting firms. SMBs lack the documented business logic AI systems get built from. Enterprises are too distributed to execute a holistic strategy. Mid-markets are systematized just enough to build against.

changeEvents.title: Middle Management Is Ending
changeEvents.description: In an AI-native company, two roles matter: ICs who build and operate, and DRIs who own outcomes. Middle management exists to coordinate, and AI does coordination now. A greenfield claim, not a prescription for legacy orgs.

changeEvents.title: Model Upgrades Are No Longer Strictly Upgrades
Only Frontier Models Replace Skilled Labor
changeEvents.description: Substituting for skilled labor means substituting for judgment and generality, which live only at the frontier. Small models automate the repetitive slivers that were never the skilled part. So skilled-labor replacement is load-bearing on frontier progress, task by task.

changeEvents.title: Open Weights Cap What Closed Labs Can Charge
changeEvents.description: Every efficiency paper an open lab publishes does two things at once: it caps what closed labs can charge, and it grows a commons that moves the moat off the technique and onto distribution, reliability, and trust.

changeEvents.title: Owners Near an Exit Are the Easiest AI Buyers
changeEvents.description: An owner heading for a sale is the easiest buyer of AI transformation, because the payout makes the return legible. Sell the work as a pre-sale remodel: a dated, quantified investment that shows up in the sale price.

changeEvents.title: Pain Tolerance for Drudgery Is a Bug
changeEvents.description: Enduring brute-force drudgery is a cost you stopped questioning, not a virtue. Redesign the workflow so you stay in flow at the highest impact, and hire the drudgery away, for yourself and for your clients.

changeEvents.title: Permissions Are the Load-Bearing Layer of a Harness
changeEvents.description: The most powerful thing you can do for an AI agent is tell it what it cannot do. Permission design as the load-bearing layer of a working harness.

changeEvents.title: Precise Procedures Are Written for the Agent
changeEvents.description: Dense procedural precision reads as over-engineering to a human skimming for the gist. It is not for the skim. It is the interface an agent executes against faithfully, and the second reader changes what good writing is.

changeEvents.title: Progressive Automation Is the Job
changeEvents.description: The highest-leverage AI work is boring. Week after week you map one more proven, money-making workflow and automate the parts that should be automated. You are not chasing a trend or building a toy. You are buying back human attention, which is sacred, one unglamorous increment at a time.

changeEvents.title: Recurring Work Belongs in Code
changeEvents.description: For any recurring process, deterministic code is near-free to run and consistent by construction. Make it the default, and treat live model generation as the metered exception you escalate to on purpose.

changeEvents.title: Simple Harnesses Keep Winning
changeEvents.description: A small core. Extensible edges. Your context under your control. The harness architecture that keeps winning as the field matures.

changeEvents.title: Small Binaries Matter
changeEvents.description: The rule is not 'no binaries in git.' Small binaries that ship with the product belong in the repo. Large regenerable derivative sets do not, and an agent will happily commit 600MB of them unless you encode the boundary.

changeEvents.title: Software Is Disposable, Context Is the Asset
changeEvents.description: Where value lives in an AI-native company. Software gets regenerated when the models get smarter. Data, skills, and captured context do not. Build for the inversion: hoard the substrate, treat the tooling as disposable.

changeEvents.title: Some of Every Role Should Never Be Automated
changeEvents.description: Some capacities stay decisively human, and in every seat a few of them are load-bearing. The jagged frontier maps where AI is strong; the comparative human edge maps the part of a role you should never try to automate.

changeEvents.title: Sometimes the Workflow Step Should Be an Agent
changeEvents.description: A single LLM call is the cheap default for a step in a workflow. When the middle of the task needs its own judgment, generated code, and a way to check its own work, put a real agent there instead.

changeEvents.title: Sovereignty Cannot Be Sold at the Expense of Safety
changeEvents.description: Understanding your stack is worth a lot, and it is not the top value. When sovereignty and safety conflict, safety wins, which is why picking a vendor whose priority order puts safety first can be a sovereign decision rather than a surrender of one.

changeEvents.title: Strategy Starts From What Will Not Change
changeEvents.description: Identifying what is durable in your industry matters as much as identifying what will be disrupted. Most consultants only sell change. Selling clients on what to protect is the differentiator.

changeEvents.title: Task Difficulty Does Not Predict AI Performance
changeEvents.description: AI capability has an uneven border. Human-perceived difficulty does not predict which tasks AI does brilliantly and which it botches. You map the border by probing it, and it moves outward every week.

changeEvents.title: The Agentic OS UX Problem Is a Packaging Problem
changeEvents.description: The capability layer of a personal agentic OS is already good enough for normal people. What they are missing is a door shaped like the software they already understand: an app. Thin app-shaped surfaces over a proven skill library dissolve most of the agentic OS UX problem.

changeEvents.title: The Best Judges of Creations Should Be Training AI
changeEvents.description: Taste is not a scale problem. A model's ceiling on any creative domain is the taste of whoever judged its output, so the highest-leverage hire in applied AI is the person whose verdict on a creation the market already trusts.

changeEvents.title: The Best Transformations Follow the Same Arc
changeEvents.description: The common process the best AI transformation engagements converge on. Refuse the one-tool instinct, lead with a ROI-ranked strategy blueprint, ship quick wins that pay back fast, then sequence the rollout so each solution compounds the last. Derived from a library of mid-market case studies.

changeEvents.title: The Chat Is Not the Product
The Cheaper Code Gets, the Simpler You Should Build
changeEvents.description: When producing code costs almost nothing, the friction that used to enforce simplicity is gone. Restraint is now something you supply on purpose. Build the simplest thing that works, and stop.

changeEvents.title: The Generator Is the Only Thing Worth Fixing
changeEvents.description: When a system you own produces the wrong result, the fix belongs in the system, not the artifact. The intended outcome is the authority, so a rule that blocks it is a bug in the generator, not a constraint to route around.

changeEvents.title: The GUI Is Becoming Legacy
changeEvents.description: The graphic user interface was the human-friendly wrapper around the computer. The wrapper is being unwound. The capability is moving back to where it always lived: the terminal.

changeEvents.title: The Harness Is the Thing Worth Learning
changeEvents.description: Agentic harnesses (Claude Code, Hermes, Codex) are primitives. Vendor wrappers over them (Claude Cowork, opinionated desktop apps) hide those primitives to look friendlier. We teach the primitives,...

changeEvents.title: The Human Role Splits Into Instigator and Editor
changeEvents.description: The human role in AI-native work splits into two anchors: instigators who kick off the work and define what success looks like, and editors who curate the output and decide what ships. The agent fills the middle.

changeEvents.title: The Magnificent Crash Is Coming
changeEvents.description: A large market correction is coming because there is far more AI technology than there is guidance to deploy it. The valuations assume a transformation that trust, which forms slowly, cannot deliver on the implied schedule.

changeEvents.title: The Self-Improving Business Is a Bad Meme
changeEvents.description: A direct rebuttal to the recursive-self-improving-business framing. Workflows can self-update; businesses do not self-improve. The human is the improver. Implementers who consult from any other premise ship the wrong shape.

changeEvents.title: There Is No Standing Still Anymore
Throughput Without Taste Is a Slop Factory
Tokens Are Cheap, Your Future Attention Is Not
changeEvents.description: An agent left to optimize for the cheapest completion of this turn will quietly spend your scarcest resource: the attention it costs you to review work that came back wrong, and the attention it costs future you to rediscover a lesson nobody wrote down.

changeEvents.title: Tokens Are the Atomic Unit of AI Economics
Too Many Early Pilots Will Drown You
changeEvents.description: Signing too many pilot customers early drowns you in human labor before you can build the product to scale, so you stay stuck using humans. The fix is counterintuitive: cap your first pilots to a small handful.

changeEvents.title: Trust Attaches to Operators With a Named Framework
changeEvents.description: Productize your service as a signature named framework. The Big-4 pattern (McKinsey, BCG, Bain) is the reference. "I'll build whatever you want" sounds accommodating but reads as not-standing-on-anything. Trust attaches to operators with an opinion.

changeEvents.title: Variance Is the Existential Problem
changeEvents.description: Customers fire an AI-services company for inconsistent output faster than for being slower or more expensive than the incumbent. Consistency is what they are buying. Output variance, not speed or price, is the churn driver.

changeEvents.title: Vendor Resistance Is a Revealed-Preference Problem
changeEvents.description: What you already use is the real statement of your values. Every device, service, and account you run says you accepted big-tech dependence long ago. The AI stack is where you noticed.

changeEvents.title: Vertical Integration Is the Moat
changeEvents.description: Model quality converges, but the harness compounds. The company that fully verticalizes the model and the harness harvests the one dataset nobody else has: how humans turn intent into action and whether they got what they wanted. Users pay to train it, and productizing the harness as an SDK farms that collection out to other companies too.

changeEvents.title: Vice Is Quantifiable
changeEvents.description: Vice has a clear objective function. Virtue does not. This is why AI monetizes in vice first, and why any attempt to build a wisdom-optimizing AI runs into a fundamental mathematical floor.

changeEvents.title: Wisdom Is the Only Durable AI Defense
changeEvents.description: Classical formation in virtue and wisdom is the only durable response to AI's degradation of human cognitive capacity. The argument is not anti-technology. It is pro-human-depth.

changeEvents.title: You Are Having the 2008 Cloud Argument Again
changeEvents.description: Managed agent platforms are running the cloud's play: not making infrastructure better, making owning it optional. The objections to the cloud were correct and lost anyway, and why they lost decides what you keep portable this time.

changeEvents.title: You Cannot Acquire Product-Market Fit
changeEvents.description: Buying a legacy services firm and bolting AI on top is a trap: you cannot acquire product-market fit, and legacy expectations on metrics, hiring, and performance do not change because you added AI. The one exception is a regulatory moat you need fast.

changeEvents.title: You Cannot Plan the Upgrades That Matter
changeEvents.description: The features that make a generation pipeline good are discovered by delivering real artifacts to real people, not by designing the pipeline up front. Real delivery is the roadmap, and the commit history is the record of thinking.

changeEvents.title: You Cannot Reason About AI You Have Not Felt
You Can't Distill Your Way to the Frontier
changeEvents.description: Distilling a model from another model's outputs reproduces the teacher's surface answers while inheriting its errors. You can copy the frontier cheaply, but you cannot lead from a copy: the durable edge belongs to the models trained closest to reality.

changeEvents.title: Your Computer Was Always Underused
changeEvents.description: The bottleneck on your computer was never the hardware. It was that you could not translate intent into bash. A coding agent that masters the shell finally puts the machine you already own to work.

changeEvents.title: Your Edge Is Not Your Infrastructure
changeEvents.description: A subject-matter expert going all-in on AI should own the judgment, the taste, and the outcome, not invent a harness and a deployment. The infrastructure is the part someone else has already solved better.

changeEvents.title: Your First Touch Should Sell the Next Step, Not the Product
changeEvents.description: A cold reader gives you seconds and no benefit of the doubt, so the first message cannot carry your argument. Its only job is to earn the next step, and proof does that where explanation does not.

changeEvents.title: Your Highest-Leverage Writing Has an Audience of One
changeEvents.description: Three genres of writing compete for your hours: for yourself, for one person, for a crowd. The public genre is the one most practitioners practice daily and the one that pays the least. The private genre is where your read on reality gets corrected, and it is now also the substrate your agents run on.

changeEvents.title: Your Process Is Disposable, Your Judgment Is Not
changeEvents.description: The value was never the process. It was the outcome. The process was only the cheapest known path to it, and clinging to it blinds you when a cheaper or better way to generate the outcome appears.

changeEvents.title: Your Reader Already Has the Objection
changeEvents.description: Anyone technical enough to matter already knows the counterargument to what you are recommending. Stating it in its strongest form, before they raise it, is what earns you the right to answer it.

changeEvents.title: Evals
changeEvents.description: The discipline of measuring AI output quality at a level the operator can actually trust. Golden sets, rubrics, regression rules.

changeEvents.title: Legible Organization
changeEvents.description: Record everything so the AI can see it. If it was not captured, it did not happen to your intelligence. The pre-condition for every self-improving loop. Emails, messages, meetings, office hours, decisions, hand-offs, all of it, diarized and surfaced as context.

changeEvents.title: Outside-In Plus Future-Back Strategy
changeEvents.description: Two strategy principles that separate a real AI strategy from a prioritized backlog. Outside-in starts from market drivers, not current workflows. Future-back works backward from the wave-3 system to today's investments.

changeEvents.title: AI Opportunity Radar
changeEvents.description: A brainstorming tool for surfacing AI strategy moves you would otherwise miss. For each AI capability, generate first-order possibilities and second-order possibilities. The second-order column is where wave-3 strategy lives.

changeEvents.title: The AI Tech Partnership Revenue Model
changeEvents.description: Budget plus a percentage of top-line revenue. Borrowed from the growth-marketing partner model and adapted for AI consulting. Aligns incentives, captures the value AI labor replacement actually produces, and re-rates the consulting firm's revenue quality.

changeEvents.title: Archive, Never Delete
changeEvents.description: Clear a cluttered workspace by sweeping loose files into a dated archive folder, not by deleting them. Cheap storage makes every file you have ever touched a recoverable part of your context corpus. Pruning is a separate, deliberate decision.

changeEvents.title: Audit to Sprint to Deployment
changeEvents.description: The Forward Deployed Engineer's engagement loop: open with an audit that maps the real work and its ROI, prove behavior with evals, then deploy on top of existing systems. Improving one workflow makes the next one obvious, so the loop compounds.

changeEvents.title: The Capture-First Autobiography
changeEvents.description: Capture the raw truth of a life into files you own before turning any of it into a book, a site, or a video. A continuous AI interview builds the corpus; every format you ever want is a projection of it.

changeEvents.title: Convert the Pilot to an Engagement
changeEvents.description: Structure a paid three-month POC so the year-long engagement is almost automatic. The MBB wedge, copyable by any boutique that can execute the shape.

changeEvents.title: Decompose the Workflow
changeEvents.description: Draw the entire business as one linear workflow, decompose to irreducible actions, then classify each one as automatable, augmentable, or human-only.

changeEvents.title: Deploy a Slide Deck as a Website
changeEvents.description: How to build a slide deck as a page on your own website: one fixed-proportion canvas that scales to fit any screen (so a phone shows a perfect miniature of the projector view, never a reflowed mess), click left and right to navigate like presenter view, exports to a crisp PDF from the same code, and is built by applying the brand OS.

changeEvents.title: Don't scale slop
changeEvents.description: Automating a broken process gives you broken at 10x speed. Fix the process and build infrastructure before AI.

changeEvents.title: Engineer the First Hour
changeEvents.description: Engineering the first hour with a visionary entrepreneur so they cross from 'this exists' to 'this is the lever I have been missing.' Without that crossing, nothing downstream compounds.

changeEvents.title: Be an applied AI scientist
changeEvents.description: The best implementers don't think like plumbers. They think like scientists: hypothesis, measurement, iteration, raw data.

changeEvents.title: Finding clients through trust
changeEvents.description: The number-one mistake implementers make is cold-pitching strangers on AI consulting. Here's what actually works.

changeEvents.title: Make Every Share Link an Invite
changeEvents.description: A viral-invite and attribution-graph pattern for gated products: every member's share link doubles as an invite, every new member is permanently attributed to whoever brought them, and the result is a legacy tree instead of a marketing funnel.

changeEvents.title: Nail Your ICP First
changeEvents.description: Get rigorously honest about who you serve before you build anything. Most AI adoption problems are clarity problems wearing a tooling costume.

changeEvents.title: Package the Patterns You Keep Copying
changeEvents.description: When you have copied the same code into a third project, publish it as a package so a fix is one update instead of many.

changeEvents.title: Picking an AI-Services Market
changeEvents.description: A four-trait filter for choosing the market to build an AI-native services company in: low trust, low judgment at the task level, a high intelligence threshold, and regulation as a moat. Plus two checks: the Sam Altman test and the no-physical-ops rule.

changeEvents.title: Pitch the Pilot
changeEvents.description: Propose your first engagement as a small, well-scoped pilot that is almost impossible for the client to say no to.

changeEvents.title: Pricing AI engagements
changeEvents.description: Price by the transformation, not by the hour. A framework for thinking through pricing on any applied AI engagement.

changeEvents.title: Scope the Pilot
changeEvents.description: Define the concrete bounded experiment that proves or disproves whether AI delivers real value for a specific part of the business.

changeEvents.title: Stand Up an Eval Harness in Week One
changeEvents.description: Stand up the minimum viable eval loop on a new engagement so quality is measured from day one, not discovered three months in.

changeEvents.title: Version-Control Your Prompts
changeEvents.description: Every AI prompt that produced something worth keeping is source code. Store it in a file you own, port it across models, sharpen it over time. For image prompts, alt text is the storage vector that pulls double duty as accessibility.

changeEvents.title: Workshop → Blueprint → Project → Partnership Engagement Ladder
changeEvents.description: The four-step engagement structure that takes AI consulting contracts from $5k to $1M+. Each step is a fixed-price offer. Each step builds trust before the next step gets pitched. Custom AI Studio's operating model.

changeEvents.title: Agent Constellation
changeEvents.description: Staffing an operation with many narrowly scoped, persistently named agents instead of one all-knowing assistant. Each one gets a job, its own tools, and its own workspace.

changeEvents.title: Agentic Brand OS
changeEvents.description: An Agentic Brand OS is the runtime that loads a brand's version-controlled cartridge (its canon and blessed goldens) and renders any on-brand asset from it, so an agent produces new sites, decks, and assets that all land in the same brand universe.

changeEvents.title: Agentic Brand Universe
changeEvents.description: A portable, version-controlled brand packaged as data: its canon (characters, settings, motifs, voice, rules) plus its blessed golden assets, held in a form an agent can load and render from. The cartridge in a three-layer ontology where the Agentic Brand OS is the console that loads it and a deliverable is the projection it renders.

changeEvents.title: Agentic Project Management
changeEvents.description: Holding a project as a repo an agent can read: every piece of context in files, a resumable state machine, the project's verbs as skills, and a supervising subagent that answers what is next. Version control, source control and resumability stop being features to build and arrive for free.

changeEvents.title: Agentic UX Rules
changeEvents.description: A growing list of UX rules for the agentic age. The bar for product UX has moved because AI moved it.

changeEvents.title: AI Developer Workflow
changeEvents.description: The real unit of agentic engineering: a repeatable composition of engineers, agents, and code that runs a piece of work end to end. The loop is one node inside it. Composed up behind a router, many of them become a software factory.

changeEvents.title: The AI-Native Services Company
changeEvents.description: A services firm rebuilt from scratch so AI does most of the work and the company delivers the finished outcome instead of a copilot. The opposite of SaaS: you absorb the whole job and hand back the result. Trillion-dollar markets that did not exist two years ago.

changeEvents.title: AI Operating Leverage
changeEvents.description: The P&L bet of an AI-native services company: the more the product is built, the lower the cost of goods sold and the better the gross margin. It is what pulls a services firm from a ~30% margin ceiling toward software-like 50%+ on a market two to three times bigger than software.

changeEvents.title: Anxious Creativity
changeEvents.description: The compulsion to be doing something with AI without knowing what. It reads as creativity and feels like progress, but it is anxiety: a fear of falling behind that pulls you off the proven work you already do well into an endless churn of new tools and half-built experiments.

changeEvents.title: Business Logic as AI System
changeEvents.description: The meta-pattern underneath almost every AI consulting engagement. Take the logic of the business, whether it's been written down or not, and convert it into an AI system. Naming the pattern changes how you scope, sell, price, and execute.

changeEvents.title: Campaign Plugins
changeEvents.description: A plugin is the right container for a campaign: skills as the campaign's atomic actions, versioned files as its state machine, layered on top of the permanent relationship record. The operator talks; the campaign updates itself.

changeEvents.title: Cognitive Coverage
changeEvents.description: Like test coverage measures how much of your code is exercised by tests, cognitive coverage measures how much of an agent's work you actually understand. Verify understanding, do not just accept output.

changeEvents.title: Deep Provenance
changeEvents.description: Recording what produced every artifact, in enough detail that you can tell which input to change. Without it you re-roll and hope. With it you steer, and you also learn which finished work a changed input made suspect.

changeEvents.title: Digital Employee
changeEvents.description: A domain expert's packaged judgment, rentable as a product: the new category agent SDKs unlock, where the expertise scales past the expert's calendar.

changeEvents.title: Gain Sharing
changeEvents.description: Charging a share of the measurable gain you create, the savings you uncover or the upside you unlock, instead of a share of your time. The fee floats with the result.

changeEvents.title: The Generative Welcome
changeEvents.description: A paste-in recipe a practitioner hands a prospect, who runs it inside their own AI harness to generate a personalized, on-brand artifact showing what AI could do for their specific business, plus a warm introduction to the practitioner. The generic funnel becomes a one-to-one, self-serve aha the prospect experiences by pasting one file.

changeEvents.title: Golden Atomic Brand References (GABRs)
changeEvents.description: A curated set of reference images that carry a brand's recurring visual identity (character looks, style anchors, palette, motifs) into every image-generation request. Passed alongside the prompt, they solve the drift problem: identity rides in image data, not text description.

changeEvents.title: Golden Chain
changeEvents.description: The method for building a set of assets that must agree with each other: generate one at a time, conditioning each new asset on the blessed seed plus every asset accepted before it. Parallel generation produces variations that share a description; a chain produces one subject seen from many angles.

changeEvents.title: Golden Processes
changeEvents.description: Golden is a status for how you make things, not only for the artifacts you keep. A golden process is a human-blessed, version-controlled procedure that reliably turns a small amount of the right human input into an excellent result.

changeEvents.title: Golden
changeEvents.description: A status a human confers, not a quality an artifact has on its own. An artifact is golden when a person with authority to set the bar has approved it as canon and promoted it into the version-controlled library where it becomes load-bearing on all future work.

changeEvents.title: Hand-Rolling
changeEvents.description: Producing a one-off result by hand to get around your own system, instead of improving the system so it produces the result. Every hand-roll is a fix that helps once and teaches the generator nothing.

changeEvents.title: Hyperdocumented SOP
changeEvents.description: An SOP documented for double duty: a human can follow it and an agent can execute it. The unit of workflow documentation that makes progressive automation possible. Awareness page; the canonical standard lives on the truth-management wiki.

changeEvents.title: Idempotent Steps
changeEvents.description: A step is idempotent when running it a second time is safe and changes nothing. In agentic work, where sessions crash, run out of context, and get interrupted constantly, idempotency converts crash recovery from a design problem into a non-problem: the recovery procedure is just run it again.

changeEvents.title: In-Context Learning
changeEvents.description: The only lever you have. You cannot touch the model's weights, so every customization enters as text in the context window. Which turns agent customization into context engineering under a fixed budget.

changeEvents.title: In, On, and Out of the Loop
changeEvents.description: Three positions a human can hold relative to an automated workflow: in the loop (the human is the gate), on the loop (the human supervises), out of the loop (fully automated, no human trigger). Good practice graduates each workflow down the loop as capability advances.

changeEvents.title: Masturbatory Programming
changeEvents.description: Building technical systems as self-expression instead of service, so the builder's identity attaches to the architecture rather than to anyone it was supposed to serve. The tell is a detailed system and zero users.

changeEvents.title: The Mission Harness
changeEvents.description: Everyone talks about AI alignment. Aligned to what? A mission harness makes it concrete: a system that keeps humans and agents aligned with a shared purpose.

changeEvents.title: Neurosymbolic AI
changeEvents.description: Wiring a probabilistic neural model to a formal symbolic layer (an ontology, a rule set, a type system) so the parts that must be exact get checked by something that cannot hallucinate. The name for the architecture reliable agent systems keep converging on.

changeEvents.title: Paving the Desire Path
changeEvents.description: The retrospective pass over a finished run that finds the hand-rolls you could not see while making them, and hardens the ones you have already walked more than once into reusable components. You do not plan a desire path, you discover it by looking at where the grass actually died.

changeEvents.title: Plugins
changeEvents.description: The packaging and distribution layer for agent extensions: a per-vendor bundle of skills, commands, subagents, hooks, and MCP servers, installed from a marketplace. The plugin is the box; MCP is the cargo.

changeEvents.title: Project Resumability
changeEvents.description: The property that lets a reader who was not there reach a project's true state in minutes, from the files alone, and be right about it. Saving is the act, agentic project management is one implementation, resumability is the quality both are trying to produce.

changeEvents.title: Prompt Guards
changeEvents.description: Standing rules a generator appends to every prompt itself, conditional on what the prompt contains. A rule written as an instruction to the caller is a suggestion; a rule enforced at the chokepoint every caller passes through is a guarantee.

changeEvents.title: Propaganda-Weighted Average
changeEvents.description: The average of the public internet is the world's pitch, not the world's truth. Models trained on it inherit that weighting. Vague prompts collapse to the propaganda-weighted average; specific prompts with operator ground-truth context pull away from it.

changeEvents.title: Ratcheting Standards
changeEvents.description: A check that records how many violations a codebase already has and fails only when the number goes up. Lets you adopt a standard today on a codebase that does not meet it, without blocking on a cleanup you will keep postponing.

changeEvents.title: Reverse Centaur
changeEvents.description: An AI deployment that inverts the centaur: the human is subordinated to the machine, paced by it, deskilled by it, and left to absorb the blame when it fails. The failure mode applied AI adoption should be designed against.

changeEvents.title: The Roles-to-Workflows Shift
changeEvents.description: Stop thinking about your business in terms of roles. Start thinking in terms of workflows. The single biggest mental model shift for the AI era.

changeEvents.title: Seat Wrapper
changeEvents.description: A purpose-built AI system scoped to one seat, encoding that role's repeatable processes so the person spends their hours in their comparative human edge. The good kind of wrapper: narrow, specific, built on the primitive.

changeEvents.title: Spare Cycles
changeEvents.description: A standing backlog of non-urgent, high-value work you pull from whenever you have surplus capacity to spend, so idle compute compounds instead of evaporating.

changeEvents.title: Spikes
changeEvents.description: A small, throwaway experiment whose only job is to kill one risky unknown before you build the real thing. In agentic development its value is the question it answers, never the code it leaves behind.

changeEvents.title: The AI Question
changeEvents.description: The single question every leader is actually asking about AI right now: how can I use it to become more successful? Meet them there, or every high-ticket engagement is out of order.

changeEvents.title: The Billing Adapter
changeEvents.description: A seam that separates what AI work costs from who pays for it, so one product can bill each request to the right wallet.

changeEvents.title: The Corpus and the Projection
changeEvents.description: Every generated artifact fuses two things: the corpus of annotated inputs and intent it draws from, and the projection, the editable spec that turns that corpus into this particular artifact. Separate them and the corpus becomes a durable asset while every artifact stays cheap, re-rollable, and traceable to its exact source.

changeEvents.title: The Doctor Pattern
changeEvents.description: Give an agent an explicit rubric that IS your definition of done, then loop it: grade, fix the highest-impact gap, re-grade, repeat.

changeEvents.title: The Goldilocks Pace
changeEvents.description: The operating pace that maximizes returns while keeping risk bounded, held predictably week after week.

changeEvents.title: The Harness and the Deployment
changeEvents.description: Two independent questions decide who owns an agent system: who supplies the harness, and who supplies the deployment. Teams conflate the two and end up owning both by accident.

changeEvents.title: The Outcome Economy
changeEvents.description: An economy where the sellable unit is an outcome generator: a system that embeds superintelligence to reliably produce a valued outcome on demand. You buy or integrate a generator, not a tool and not labor.

changeEvents.title: The Personalizing Factory
changeEvents.description: Superintelligent automation for personalized output. A production line that holds PRINCIPLES constant instead of a template, so the things it makes can be genuinely new and still reliably good.

changeEvents.title: The Portability Tax
changeEvents.description: The ongoing cost of keeping maximal model and vendor flexibility: building to the lowest common denominator, owning the harness and the deployment yourself, and forfeiting the platform-native capabilities that would otherwise be free.

changeEvents.title: The Product as Operation
changeEvents.description: In AI services the human is the interface to the customer and the software exists to let that human scale nonlinearly. So you build with an operations mindset: find the bottleneck, build for the bottleneck, and track throughput and cycle time like DAU.

changeEvents.title: The Prompt Factory
changeEvents.description: Deterministic code that assembles the final prompt from locked parts plus per-run variables, so no LLM call is spent constructing what a template and a branch could have built.

changeEvents.title: The Renderer and the Payload
changeEvents.description: Every generated artifact is two things fused by default: the presentation and the content. Host the renderer once, let the content travel as data, and the cost, the shelf life, and the privacy of the artifact all change at once.

changeEvents.title: The Sam Altman Test
changeEvents.description: A one-line diagnostic for model risk: as the models get better, does your service get stronger, or does the model itself commoditize you? Build only where capability jumps are tailwinds.

changeEvents.title: The Session Save
changeEvents.description: The deliberate act of routing a work session's hard-won value (decisions, rationale, and newly-earned tribal knowledge) into durable homes (work logs, skill files, wiki pages, memory, commits) before the chat clears or the context window fills. The save mechanic for the playable harness experience: a reviewed sweep, never autopilot.

changeEvents.title: The Tool-Agent Category Error
changeEvents.description: LLMs do not fit cleanly into either existing ontological category. Not a tool, because we do not use them as tools. Not an agent, because they have no genuine autonomy or interests of their own. This classification failure has practical consequences.

changeEvents.title: The Three Actors of Value Creation
changeEvents.description: Engineering value now comes from three actors: engineers, agents, and code. The craft is placing each in the right node. Ranked by reliability it goes code, then engineers, then agents, and code is the one everyone forgets.

changeEvents.title: Transformation as Surgery
changeEvents.description: An AI transformation is invasive, expensive, and often irreversible, like surgery. The guide who profits from recommending it carries a conflict of interest, so the honest one qualifies hard before cutting.

changeEvents.title: A Moved Measurable Is the Only Proof
changeEvents.description: The proof your AI work is real is that it moves a load-bearing, profit-tied measurable the business already agreed matters. Everything else is novelty at best, and AI is happy to help you mistake it for traction.

changeEvents.title: Agents Compress Work Onto Your Judgment
changeEvents.description: AI agents do not reduce work. They compress it. The compression lands on the one layer that does not scale: human judgment.

changeEvents.title: AGI Is Already Here for People Who Can Wield It
AI Discourse Refuses to Name Its Political Reality
changeEvents.description: The obvious political reality that AI discourse keeps refusing to name: the flaming red elephant in the room. Red for the revolutionary spirit rising in a generation locked out of the economy. Flaming for the firebombs already being thrown at AI executives and data centers. Elephant because the cause is obvious and nobody at the top of the industry wants to look at it.

changeEvents.title: AI Is Becoming the Thing We Serve
changeEvents.description: We built AI to serve us. We are ending up serving it. The ancient pattern of the idol is playing out in real time: the thing made to extend human power becomes the thing humans serve.

changeEvents.title: AI-Native Org Charts Put Humans at the Edges
changeEvents.description: In an AI-native company, the AI sits in the center: the company brain, the data, the skills, the loops. Humans live at the perimeter, interfacing with reality where the intelligence makes contact with the world. The org chart inverts.

changeEvents.title: Applied AI Pays Off Where Fit Is Already Proven
changeEvents.description: Applied AI pays off fastest inside a business that has already proven market fit, where it clears bottlenecks and compounds profit. Spinning up a speculative AI startup in today's crowded, bubbly market is a far worse use of the same energy.

changeEvents.title: Buyers Fumble Alone Before They Hire You
changeEvents.description: People try to figure out AI alone on minimal spend, fumble for months, then hire a coach. The lag between starting solo and reaching out is the consultant's sales-timing signal.

changeEvents.title: Capability Is Table Stakes, Faithfulness Is the Choice
changeEvents.description: The bar for choosing an agentic stack is faithfulness: acting in the spirit of your mission when your instructions run out, and sometimes holding you to a higher standard than you asked for.

changeEvents.title: Crossing $5M Revenue Re-Rates a Services Firm
changeEvents.description: Services businesses sell at 1-2x EBITDA below roughly $5M annual revenue and 4-5x EBITDA above it. The same multiple jump applies to AI consulting firms. The threshold is the structural reason the exit posture decision matters.

changeEvents.title: Developers Have Started Worshipping the Build
changeEvents.description: Developers have started worshipping the act of building over the outcome it is supposed to serve. Spending tokens feels like progress. It is not. The business only ever paid for the outcome, and most of the outcome is already solved.

changeEvents.title: Efficiency Wins Do Not Predict New-Category Wins
changeEvents.description: AI adoption follows the same three-wave shape every prior general-purpose technology took. Wave 1 squeezes efficiency from existing workflows. Wave 2 raises quality. Wave 3 invents new categories. Wave 1 success does not predict Wave 3 success.

changeEvents.title: Every AI Business Model Has a Different Ceiling
changeEvents.description: A working chart of every distinct business model for monetizing AI expertise in 2026, plotted on technical depth against contract size. Each model has a different ceiling, a different exit profile, and a different operational shape. Pick deliberately.

changeEvents.title: Every Company Is Quietly Sorting Its People
Execution Is No Longer What You Get Paid For
changeEvents.description: Daniel Priestley's framing of post-AI work. AI tokens replace task execution, so humans get paid for conviction, judgment, taste, commercial outcomes, and improving the system.

changeEvents.title: Generation Is Cheap, Discrimination Is the Job
Great Work Is a Byproduct of Volume Plus Taste
Lifestyle or Enterprise Value Is a Day-One Decision
changeEvents.description: The decision every AI consulting founder makes in their first month, usually without naming it. Lifestyle businesses and enterprise-value businesses look the same on day 30 and look completely different on day 730. Choose deliberately.

changeEvents.title: LLMs Handle Judgment, Code Handles Everything Else
Making One Layer Cheap Just Moves the Bottleneck
changeEvents.description: Make one layer cheap and the binding constraint does not disappear. It relocates. Efficiency is a frontier you keep advancing, not a finish line you cross once.

changeEvents.title: Mid-Market Executives Are Buying a Narrative
changeEvents.description: Mid-market executives are not buying AI systems. They are buying a coherent narrative they can take to their board, their team, and themselves. The technology is downstream of the narrative. Once you see this, your sales calls change.

changeEvents.title: Middle Management Is Ending
changeEvents.description: In an AI-native company, two roles matter: ICs who build and operate, and DRIs who own outcomes. Middle management exists to coordinate, and AI does coordination now. A greenfield claim, not a prescription for legacy orgs.

changeEvents.title: Model Upgrades Are No Longer Strictly Upgrades
Open Weights Cap What Closed Labs Can Charge
changeEvents.description: Every efficiency paper an open lab publishes does two things at once: it caps what closed labs can charge, and it grows a commons that moves the moat off the technique and onto distribution, reliability, and trust.

changeEvents.title: Pain Tolerance for Drudgery Is a Bug
changeEvents.description: Enduring brute-force drudgery is a cost you stopped questioning, not a virtue. Redesign the workflow so you stay in flow at the highest impact, and hire the drudgery away, for yourself and for your clients.

changeEvents.title: Permissions Are the Load-Bearing Layer of a Harness
changeEvents.description: The most powerful thing you can do for an AI agent is tell it what it cannot do. Permission design as the load-bearing layer of a working harness.

changeEvents.title: Recurring Work Belongs in Code
changeEvents.description: For any recurring process, deterministic code is near-free to run and consistent by construction. Make it the default, and treat live model generation as the metered exception you escalate to on purpose.

changeEvents.title: Simple Harnesses Keep Winning
changeEvents.description: A small core. Extensible edges. Your context under your control. The harness architecture that keeps winning as the field matures.

changeEvents.title: Software Is Disposable, Context Is the Asset
changeEvents.description: Where value lives in an AI-native company. Software gets regenerated when the models get smarter. Data, skills, and captured context do not. Build for the inversion: hoard the substrate, treat the tooling as disposable.

changeEvents.title: Some of Every Role Should Never Be Automated
changeEvents.description: Some capacities stay decisively human, and in every seat a few of them are load-bearing. The jagged frontier maps where AI is strong; the comparative human edge maps the part of a role you should never try to automate.

changeEvents.title: Strategy Starts From What Will Not Change
changeEvents.description: Identifying what is durable in your industry matters as much as identifying what will be disrupted. Most consultants only sell change. Selling clients on what to protect is the differentiator.

changeEvents.title: Task Difficulty Does Not Predict AI Performance
changeEvents.description: AI capability has an uneven border. Human-perceived difficulty does not predict which tasks AI does brilliantly and which it botches. You map the border by probing it, and it moves outward every week.

changeEvents.title: The Best Transformations Follow the Same Arc
changeEvents.description: The common process the best AI transformation engagements converge on. Refuse the one-tool instinct, lead with a ROI-ranked strategy blueprint, ship quick wins that pay back fast, then sequence the rollout so each solution compounds the last. Derived from a library of mid-market case studies.

changeEvents.title: The Generator Is the Only Thing Worth Fixing

changeEvents.title: Goldratt: management attention is the ultimate constraint

changeEvents.title: Making One Layer Cheap Just Moves the Bottleneck

changeEvents.title: Agents Read READMEs

changeEvents.title: Reverse Centaur

changeEvents.title: Cory Doctorow

changeEvents.title: The AI Guidance Gap
changeEvents.description: The structural gap between how fast AI capability ships and how slowly the human trust, judgment, and capability needed to deploy it actually form. The gap caps adoption, and it is the opportunity.

changeEvents.title: The AI Question

changeEvents.title: Transformation as Surgery

changeEvents.title: The Magnificent Crash Is Coming
changeEvents.description: A large market correction is coming because there is far more AI technology than there is guidance to deploy it. The valuations assume a transformation that trust, which forms slowly, cannot deliver on the implied schedule.

changeEvents.title: The AI-Native Services Company
changeEvents.description: A services firm rebuilt from scratch so AI does most of the work and the company delivers the finished outcome instead of a copilot. The opposite of SaaS: you absorb the whole job and hand back the result. Trillion-dollar markets that did not exist two years ago.

changeEvents.title: AI Operating Leverage
changeEvents.description: The P&L bet of an AI-native services company: the more the product is built, the lower the cost of goods sold and the better the gross margin. It is what pulls a services firm from a ~30% margin ceiling toward software-like 50%+ on a market two to three times bigger than software.

changeEvents.title: The Product as Operation
changeEvents.description: In AI services the human is the interface to the customer and the software exists to let that human scale nonlinearly. So you build with an operations mindset: find the bottleneck, build for the bottleneck, and track throughput and cycle time like DAU.

changeEvents.title: The Sam Altman Test
changeEvents.description: A one-line diagnostic for model risk: as the models get better, does your service get stronger, or does the model itself commoditize you? Build only where capability jumps are tailwinds.

changeEvents.title: You Cannot Acquire Product-Market Fit
changeEvents.description: Buying a legacy services firm and bolting AI on top is a trap: you cannot acquire product-market fit, and legacy expectations on metrics, hiring, and performance do not change because you added AI. The one exception is a regulatory moat you need fast.

changeEvents.title: Too Many Early Pilots Will Drown You
changeEvents.description: Signing too many pilot customers early drowns you in human labor before you can build the product to scale, so you stay stuck using humans. The fix is counterintuitive: cap your first pilots to a small handful.

changeEvents.title: Variance Is the Existential Problem
changeEvents.description: Customers fire an AI-services company for inconsistent output faster than for being slower or more expensive than the incumbent. Consistency is what they are buying. Output variance, not speed or price, is the churn driver.

changeEvents.title: Picking an AI-Services Market
changeEvents.description: A four-trait filter for choosing the market to build an AI-native services company in: low trust, low judgment at the task level, a high intelligence threshold, and regulation as a moat. Plus two checks: the Sam Altman test and the no-physical-ops rule.
